source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Hi, here is the document covering the first of the 3 boards. Please share your thoughts and let me know whether it makes sense.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: I believe the next 2 boards are considerably simpler. One is a standard ESP32-S3, while the other is basically just connectors for sensors.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Yes, that is right. The main board includes:

- ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N16R8 module
- INA219 current monitor on the 3.3V rail
- USB-C connector for programming, plus an LDO for standalone operation
- Every JST connector for the power board, sensor board, display, PIR, touch, LEDs, buttons, and reset
- Supporting passives, including decoupling caps, pull-ups, series resistors, Schottky diodes, and the BOOT button

It has no sensors or power management, as those are located on the other boards.

value_updates.main_board_role: ESP32-S3 processing, 3.3V current monitoring, USB programming and standalone regulation, and system connectors

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: I was thinking that, if you have availability for another project and are interested, we could create the cheapest possible single board for this project. Everything would be placed on one board, and from the beginning we would try to use JLCPCB Basica components (as much as possible). There would be far fewer connectors because interboard connectors would no longer be needed. If you have ideas for making anything better or less expensive while retaining the same functionality, you can suggest them. I can create a new milestone within this project, and we can agree on the price. What do you think—does this approach make sense?

value_updates.integrated_board_variant: place the project circuitry on one board
